page.overview:
Who is Braun?

Braun was a criminal operative of the secretive criminal organisation, SPECTRE, and a guard of Ernst Stavro Blofeld's clinical allergy-research institute atop Piz Gloria in the Swiss Alps. A minor antagonist portrayed by the late British stuntman and actor, George Lane Cooper, the character appeared in the 1969 James Bond film, On Her Majesty's Secret Service.

Braun is first seen during James Bond's arrival at Piz Gloria under the alias of Sir Hilary Bray. After rolling out a ring-holed rubber mat to keep the two from slipping over, he proceeds to help Fräulein Bunt and "Bray" out of the helicopter. Looking at the guard's sidearm, Bond comments "Fräulein, I should warn you guns make me very nervous." To which Bunt attempts to reassure the apparently nervous genealogist that they are to keep spies from rivalling companies. During dinner, Braun is seen serving as a waiter.

Later in the film, with fellow guard Felsen, he accompanies Bunt in her pursuit of the escaping Bond through the Swiss village of Lauterbrunnen. After Bond gives his location away in a shed by accidentally backing into a some hanging bells, both men brawl with the spy, but are overpowered by him. Although knocked to the floor by Bond, the pair are found by Bunt and ordered to continue the pursuit.

Escaping, 007 attempts to mingle in with the crowds near the village ice rink. As Braun and Bunt close in on him, he is approached by his girlfriend, Tracy, who leads him to her car. With Bunt's driver recognising Bond as they drive off, the thugs return to their car and set off in pursuit, almost killing the spy as he attempts to use a phone-box to communicate with London.
